note: The single definition of what a credential looks like. scripts/secret-audit.mjs scans the repository with the `audit` scope; scripts/release/gate-contract.ts scans the finished staged record with the `staged` scope. Two copies of a rule are two rules that can drift, and a comment claiming they are in step is not a check.

rules.name: assigned-secret
rules.why: An assignment that carries a value. `=` only, never `:`: `FAL_KEY: z.string()` is a schema declaring that the variable exists, not a place its value was written down, and a scanner that cannot tell those apart cries wolf on every environment module. `OPENAI_API_KEY=` with nothing after it is the correct contents of `.env.example` and must stay silent.

rules.name: assigned-secret-broad
rules.why: Deliberately wider than `assigned-secret`, and deliberately NOT applied to the working tree. The staged gate record is a small machine-written object with no schema declarations in it, so the false positives that make this rule unusable as a repository-wide audit cannot occur there — and a refusal to build costs one rerun, where a leaked value costs a rotation.
